injections.name: a-site-stops-saying-what-its-runtime-words-may-hold
injections.why: the defect itself, on the tree rather than on a fixture: `list_harness` hands over one selector per target and their number is a fact about the package, so without the declaration this law goes back to answering for words it never read

injections.name: a-declaration-is-widened-to-the-flag-the-law-is-about
injections.why: DECLARING MORE COSTS MORE, which is the half that makes the declaration something other than a way to buy silence. A site that admits `--jobs` may be among its runtime words has told this law it cannot answer, and the law must say so rather than pass

injections.name: the-wrapper-a-site-declares-through-stops-being-recognised
injections.why: the site's half and the reader's half are different things to lose: the tree can say everything right and this law still be blind, which is the state it was in before R1269

injections.name: an-undeclared-hole-is-read-as-holding-no-flags
injections.why: the arm the whole asymmetry rests on. PINNED AGAINST A FIXTURE and not against the tree, because both hole-bearing commands here DO declare — aimed at the tree this comes back green and says nothing

injections.name: a-flag-a-site-declared-is-not-weighed-against-the-question
injections.why: the door reads the declaration against the law's OWN predicate, and a reader that skipped that comparison would hand back a verdict for a site that said the flag may be there — and refuse one for every site that said it may not, which is the same clause failing in both directions. THE THIRD RED IS THAT SECOND DIRECTION and it was not named until the exhaustive set asked: a command with NO hole at all has an empty declared list too, so the inverted clause refuses every clean command in the population as well
